Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-ray shows a well-circumscribed, lobulated mass at the right pulmonary hilum (indicated by arrows) without significant surrounding consolidation or cavitation. In a patient with productive cough and mild dyspnea, this appearance is characteristic of a central endobronchial tumor such as a low-grade mucoepidermoid carcinoma, which typically presents as a smooth, polypoid hilar mass causing airway obstruction symptoms.
